open_points.subject: owner session cookie
open_points.text: carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin
open_points.question: Which cookie attributes and scope implement “only to Registry's own origin,” including host/domain, path, SameSite policy, Secure behavior on local HTTP, persistence, and deletion on sign-out or expiry?
options: A host-only, HttpOnly session cookie with a fixed Registry path, SameSite policy and conditional Secure flag
A persistent cookie whose browser expiry matches the eight-hour limit
Any cookie attributes that preserve server-side session refusal
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only HttpOnly session cookie, Path=/, SameSite=Strict, Secure whenever HTTPS is used, with no persistent lifetime, and expire it on sign-out or detected session expiry.

open_points.subject: ordering concurrent owner-session requests
open_points.text: applied one at a time, in the order they reach the session
open_points.question: What event establishes the total order when concurrent requests reach different workers or become runnable simultaneously?
options: Order when Registry first receives the HTTP request
Order when the request acquires the session-state lock
Order by a sequence value carried by the browser
open_points.default_guess: Order by acquisition of one lock for that owner session.

open_points.subject: confirmation input binding
open_points.text: kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never as the values themselves; a submission's inputs are bound when their digest equals it
open_points.question: What exact typed encoding, field order, treatment of absent values, and digest algorithm define the confirmation binding?
options: A canonical typed, length-delimited encoding declared by the release
Canonical serialization of the later State 6 request schema
Concatenation of normalized textual values in a declared order
open_points.default_guess: Use a release-declared canonical typed encoding derived from the State 6 schema and hash that encoding.

open_points.subject: uploading an import file
open_points.text: Registry reads it as data (A19) and answers, without changing anything ... The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it
open_points.question: Does an accepted upload change owner-session state by storing or replacing the uploaded file, or must the upload be observational only?
options: It changes only temporary owner-session state, not the durable store
It changes nothing and the file must be resubmitted at confirmation
It changes both session state and some durable import staging state
open_points.default_guess: Treat “without changing anything” as “without changing the durable store”; keep or replace the file in owner-session state.

open_points.subject: state left by a refused import confirmation
open_points.text: A refused confirmation keeps it, and the step may be shown again ... A refused import may be retried with a corrected file; nothing of a refused attempt remains.
open_points.question: After refusal, which temporary facts remain: the uploaded file, mapping choices, pending confirmation, or none of them?
options: The uploaded file remains, the one-time confirmation is consumed or cleared under A13, and no durable import data remains
All temporary import state is discarded
Only validation refusals keep the file; transaction or conflict refusals discard it
open_points.default_guess: Keep the uploaded file in the session, consume or clear the confirmation according to A13, and interpret “nothing remains” as no durable-store change.

open_points.subject: configuration validation
open_points.question: What exact syntax, encoding, multiplicity, and admissible-value rules make each configuration item well formed before the more specific length and path checks run?
options: State 6 declares a complete configuration schema
Only presence, secret byte length, and usable filesystem paths are checked
Each item has release-defined parsing rules outside the public API specification
open_points.default_guess: Define a release-owned configuration schema and refuse any item that cannot be parsed exactly once into its declared type.

open_points.subject: first startup diagnostic
open_points.text: The checks run in one order and the first that fails stops the start: every item of rule 1 present and none unknown ... Within one check, items go in the order rule 1 lists them.
open_points.question: When the configuration has unknown items, duplicate items, several missing items, or an equality involving two secrets, which item is the first failure and which item or items does the diagnostic name?
options: Known items are checked in rule-1 order, then unknown items in a declared lexical order
Unknown and duplicate items are checked before missing known items
The diagnostic may report the whole failed check rather than one deterministic item
open_points.default_guess: Check known required items in rule-1 order, then unknown items in Unicode order; for an equality failure, name the later item in rule-1 order.

open_points.subject: 30-day backup retention after erasure
open_points.text: it deletes every kept backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before ... While the daily runs succeed, an erasure reaches the backups at most 30 days after it
open_points.question: Must a backup containing erased data disappear no later than 30 days after the erasure, or may strict age-based deletion retain it until the next daily run, almost 31 days after the erasure?
options: Delete when age is at least 30 days
Keep the strict “more than 30 days” rule and weaken the erasure bound to less than 31 days
Schedule an additional deletion exactly when each backup reaches 30 days
open_points.default_guess: Keep daily runs but delete backups whose age is at least 30 days.

open_points.subject: backup run still active at the next schedule
open_points.text: Every day at 03:00 UTC ... it makes one backup run ... Runs never overlap.
open_points.question: If the preceding run is still active at the next 03:00 UTC, is that day's run skipped, queued to start after completion, or does the existing run count as that day's run?
options: Skip the new run with no catch-up
Queue one run for immediately after the active run
Treat the active run as satisfying the new day's schedule
open_points.default_guess: Skip the overlapping scheduled run and try again at the following 03:00 UTC.

open_points.subject: cleanup of backups encrypted with an older key
open_points.text: older backups stay encrypted with the key they were made with ... it deletes ... every file under the kept prefix that cannot be read as a backup
open_points.question: Does “read as a backup” mean that its unencrypted metadata is structurally readable, or that Registry can decrypt and validate it using the currently configured key?
options: Readable metadata and valid backup framing are sufficient; an old-key backup is retained
The file must decrypt with the current key, so old-key backups are deleted
Registry must be given a key ring containing every retained backup key
open_points.default_guess: Retain an old-key backup when its unencrypted metadata and framing are readable; inability to decrypt it with the current key is not grounds for deletion.

open_points.subject: project erasure changing agent-session access versions
open_points.text: every change that moves a revision states it ... a project leaving the set by its erasure included ... The owner's actions on a session — granting, revoking, changing or clearing the active project, answering a request, ending the session — state the access version the owner saw
open_points.question: When erasing one project moves the access versions of every session that contains it, must the erasure state and check those sessions' access versions as well as the project's revision?
options: Only the project's revision is stated; affected session versions move as atomic consequences
Every affected session access version must be stated and checked
Session versions are not moved by project erasure
open_points.default_guess: Require only the project's revision and move all affected session access versions atomically without checking their prior values.

open_points.subject: store-history boundary after restoration
open_points.text: That store begins its own history from the backup ... Registry starts on it as on any store ... the log's numbering, the closed import — hold within each store's history
open_points.question: What identifies the beginning and identity of a store history when Registry cannot detect a restore and neither the store nor backup metadata carries a history identity?
options: A history is an external conceptual lineage and has no stored identity
Each restored lineage receives a persisted history identifier
The backup's existing store identity continues, so restoration does not create a distinct history
open_points.default_guess: Treat history as an external conceptual lineage with an inherited backup prefix and no identifier visible to Registry.
